Employees are forbidden from reading during quiet mornings.
Applicants must commit to at least twenty hours a week.
questions.answer: It pays two dollars less per hour than the cafe job.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Two dollars less per hour, true, but you save twenty minutes of bus fare each way and can review flashcards during quiet morning hours.

questions.key_evidence_line: Two dollars less per hour, true, but you save twenty minutes of bus fare each way
questions.explanation_zh: 第5句 Daniel 坦承书店时薪确实低两美元（Two dollars less per hour, true），随后用 but 引出省车费和可复习等优势。
distractor_reasons: 正确：与第5句 Two dollars less per hour 完全一致。
错误：书店主打白天安静时段，无需深夜加班。
错误：Daniel 明确提到可以在清闲的早上背单词卡（review flashcards）。
错误：是每周 10 小时，不是 20 小时（20 是单程公交分钟数）。

questions.stem: What does Hannah decide to do this afternoon?
options: Quit school for a semester to work full time.
Submit her availability schedule to the campus bookstore.
Ask the downtown cafe manager for a two-dollar raise.
Cancel her history seminar to catch up on sleep.
questions.answer: Submit her availability schedule to the campus bookstore.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Being able to study on the clock and sleep before midnight makes that trade-off totally worth it. I'll drop off my schedule this afternoon.

questions.key_evidence_line: I'll drop off my schedule this afternoon.
questions.explanation_zh: 第6句 Hannah 认为权衡利弊非常划算，决定今天下午就把时间表送过去（drop off my schedule -> submit her availability schedule）。
distractor_reasons: 错误：Hannah 决定换兼职是为了保住期中成绩，并非休学。
正确：drop off my schedule 对应 submit her availability schedule。
错误：文中未提向咖啡店要求加薪。
错误：未提取消历史研讨课。

listening_cases.title: Improving Speaking Fluency With Shadow Reading
listening_cases.title_zh: 长对话：用影子跟读与语音互评突破口语瓶颈

transcript_lines.speaker: Ben
transcript_lines.text: Sofia, I've been watching English films without subtitles for two months, yet I still freeze up whenever I speak in tutorial discussions.
transcript_lines.text_zh: Sofia，我已经连续两个月不看字幕看英文电影了，可在讨论课上开口时还是会卡壳。

transcript_lines.speaker: Sofia
transcript_lines.text: Watching movies trains your ear, Ben, but your mouth muscles never get practice unless you actually speak aloud.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 看电影训练的是耳朵，Ben，可如果你不真正开口读出来，口腔肌肉永远得不到锻炼。

transcript_lines.speaker: Ben
transcript_lines.text: That makes sense. Should I start attending the ninety-minute English corner on Friday nights?
transcript_lines.text_zh: 有道理。那我是不是该开始去参加周五晚上九十分钟的英语角？

transcript_lines.speaker: Sofia
transcript_lines.text: English corner helps, though beginners often stay quiet in big crowds. Try fifteen minutes of shadow reading each morning with a short podcast first.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 英语角有帮助，但初练者在人多的大场子里常不敢开口。不如先每天早上配合短播客做十五分钟影子跟读。

transcript_lines.speaker: Ben
transcript_lines.text: Shadow reading--you mean repeating right after the host to copy rhythm and linking sounds? How will I catch my own mistakes?
transcript_lines.text_zh: 影子跟读——你是说紧跟着主播复述，模仿节奏和连读吗？那我怎么发现自己的错误呢？

transcript_lines.speaker: Sofia
transcript_lines.text: Send me a one-minute voice clip after dinner, and I'll send back notes on your pronunciation while you check my Mandarin tones.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 晚饭后给我发一段一分钟的语音，我帮你标注发音问题，同时你也帮我听听我的汉语声调。

questions.stem: According to Sofia, why hasn't watching subtitle-free movies improved Ben's speaking?
options: Movies usually use outdated grammar and rare idioms.
Listening alone does not exercise the physical habit of speaking aloud.
Two months is too short to learn any foreign vocabulary.
Ben should turn subtitles back on during every film.
questions.answer: Listening alone does not exercise the physical habit of speaking aloud.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Watching movies trains your ear, Ben, but your mouth muscles never get practice unless you actually speak aloud.

questions.key_evidence_line: Watching movies trains your ear, Ben, but your mouth muscles never get practice unless you actually speak aloud.
questions.explanation_zh: 第2句 Sofia 指出问题根源：看电影只练耳朵（trains your ear），而不大声开口（speak aloud）会让口腔肌肉缺乏练习。
distractor_reasons: 错误：文中未指责电影语法过时。
正确：精确概括第2句“光听不练嘴”的因果解释。
错误：重点在于训练方式（被动输入 vs 主动输出），而非时间长短。
错误：Sofia 并未建议重新打开字幕。

questions.stem: What does Sofia recommend Ben do each morning instead of relying only on English corner?
options: Practice shadow reading with a short podcast for fifteen minutes.
Memorize ninety minutes of movie scripts before breakfast.
Organize a large discussion group on Friday nights.
Listen silently to news broadcasts while commuting.
questions.answer: Practice shadow reading with a short podcast for fifteen minutes.

evidence_anchor.text_span: English corner helps, though beginners often stay quiet in big crowds. Try fifteen minutes of shadow reading each morning with a short podcast first.

questions.key_evidence_line: Try fifteen minutes of shadow reading each morning with a short podcast first.
questions.explanation_zh: 第4句先指出大型英语角的局限（big crowds 中容易沉默），随后给出替代建议：每天早起配合短播客做 15 分钟影子跟读。
distractor_reasons: 正确：与第4句建议完全吻合。
错误：90 分钟是英语角时长，且不是背电影剧本。
错误：英语角人多恰恰是 Sofia 认为不利于开口的原因。
错误：核心要求是跟读开口（shadow reading），而非默听。

questions.stem: How will Ben and Sofia help each other with pronunciation?
options: They will attend tutorial classes together every Monday morning.
They will exchange short evening voice recordings for mutual feedback.
Sofia will write subtitles for Ben's favorite English films.
Ben will record fifteen-minute podcasts for Sofia's language club.
questions.answer: They will exchange short evening voice recordings for mutual feedback.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Send me a one-minute voice clip after dinner, and I'll send back notes on your pronunciation while you check my Mandarin tones.

questions.key_evidence_line: Send me a one-minute voice clip after dinner, and I'll send back notes on your pronunciation while you check my Mandarin tones.
questions.explanation_zh: 第6句提出语言交换互助方案：Ben 晚饭后发一分钟语音，Sofia 批注英文发音，同时 Ben 帮 Sofia 检查中文声调（Mandarin tones）。
distractor_reasons: 错误：文中未提周一早上一起上辅导课。
正确：short evening voice recordings for mutual feedback 准确概括“晚饭后互发一分钟语音纠音”。
错误：文中未提制作字幕。
错误：Ben 只发送一分钟的练习语音，并非录制 15 分钟播客。

listening_cases.title: Resisting Flash-Sale Countdown Traps
listening_cases.title_zh: 长对话：警惕线上闪购倒计时陷阱与冲动消费

transcript_lines.speaker: Owen
transcript_lines.text: Chloe, stop me before I click pay! This wireless headset is forty percent off, and the red countdown clock says only nine minutes remain.
transcript_lines.text_zh: Chloe，快在我点付款前拦住我！这款无线耳机打六折，红色倒计时显示只剩九分钟了。

transcript_lines.speaker: Chloe
transcript_lines.text: Wait a second, Owen. Didn't you buy reliable studio headphones just three months ago? Why are you suddenly shopping for another pair?
transcript_lines.text_zh: 等一下，Owen。你三个月前不是刚买了一副挺好用的监听耳机吗？怎么突然又要买一副？

transcript_lines.speaker: Owen
transcript_lines.text: I know, mine work fine, but seeing 'limited stock' and a ticking timer made me feel like losing the deal would be a huge mistake.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 我知道我那副好好的，但看到“库存有限”加上滴答走秒的倒计时，总觉得错过这波优惠太亏了。

transcript_lines.speaker: Chloe
transcript_lines.text: That's exactly how flash-sale pages hijack attention. Most stores repeat that exact discount every single holiday weekend anyway.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 闪购页面就是靠这招劫持注意力的。其实大多数商家每逢假期周末都会反复搞完全一样的折扣。

transcript_lines.speaker: Owen
transcript_lines.text: How do you stop yourself from checking out when a bright coupon banner pops up?
transcript_lines.text_zh: 那弹出醒目优惠券横幅时，你是怎么克制住不去结账的？

transcript_lines.speaker: Chloe
transcript_lines.text: I follow a forty-eight-hour cart rule: leave the item unpaid for two days, and turn off shopping app push alerts so urgency fades.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 我遵守“购物车四十八小时法则”：先把商品放着两天不付款，同时关掉购物软件推送提醒，让紧迫感自然消退。

questions.stem: Why did Owen feel tempted to buy the discounted wireless headset?
options: His old studio headphones broke after three months.
He needed wireless gear for a campus music concert.
The ticking timer and 'limited stock' warning triggered a fear of missing out.
Chloe recommended the headset model earlier that week.
questions.answer: The ticking timer and 'limited stock' warning triggered a fear of missing out.

evidence_anchor.text_span: I know, mine work fine, but seeing 'limited stock' and a ticking timer made me feel like losing the deal would be a huge mistake.

questions.key_evidence_line: seeing 'limited stock' and a ticking timer made me feel like losing the deal would be a huge mistake.
questions.explanation_zh: 第3句 Owen 承认旧耳机明明没坏（mine work fine），是“库存有限”和走秒倒计时让他产生了怕错失优惠的紧迫心理（losing the deal would be a huge mistake）。
distractor_reasons: 错误：Owen 明确说 mine work fine（耳机还好好的）。
错误：文中未提校园音乐会。
正确：准确概括第3句的消费心理诱因。
错误：Chloe 是在劝阻他下单，而非推荐购买。

questions.stem: What does Chloe imply about online flash-sale discounts?
options: They are rare opportunities that only appear once a year.
They are routinely repeated during almost every holiday weekend.
They always raise the shipping fee by forty percent.
They expire permanently after nine minutes.
questions.answer: They are routinely repeated during almost every holiday weekend.

evidence_anchor.text_span: That's exactly how flash-sale pages hijack attention. Most stores repeat that exact discount every single holiday weekend anyway.

questions.key_evidence_line: Most stores repeat that exact discount every single holiday weekend anyway.
questions.explanation_zh: 第4句 Chloe 揭穿闪购营销套路：大多数商家每个假期周末都会反复给出完全相同的折扣（repeat that exact discount every single holiday weekend），无需被假稀缺吓到。
distractor_reasons: 错误：与 Chloe 的判断相反，折扣并非一年只有一次。
正确：精准对应第4句商家反复促销的规律。
错误：40% 是耳机折扣幅度（forty percent off），不是运费涨幅。
错误：9 分钟只是页面倒计时制造的紧迫感，过后假期还会重复促销。

questions.stem: What strategy does Chloe use to avoid impulse purchases?
options: Waiting forty-eight hours before paying and disabling app alerts.
Deleting all saved payment cards for three months.
Asking roommates to approve every order over nine dollars.
Shopping only during late-night holiday sales.
questions.answer: Waiting forty-eight hours before paying and disabling app alerts.

evidence_anchor.text_span: I follow a forty-eight-hour cart rule: leave the item unpaid for two days, and turn off shopping app push alerts so urgency fades.

questions.key_evidence_line: leave the item unpaid for two days, and turn off shopping app push alerts so urgency fades.
questions.explanation_zh: 第6句 Chloe 分享两步实操办法：购物车静置 48 小时不付款（leave the item unpaid for two days）并关闭推送通知（turn off shopping app push alerts）。
distractor_reasons: 正确：精确对应第6句的两个动作。
错误：3 个月是 Owen 买旧耳机的时间，并非删银行卡。
错误：文中未提让室友审批订单。
错误：文中未建议深夜抢购。

listening_cases.title: Joining a Phone-Free Campus Walking Club
listening_cases.title_zh: 长对话：加入校园无手机散步小组缓解论文季焦虑

transcript_lines.speaker: Grace
transcript_lines.text: Liam, you've barely left your desk all week. How is your senior thesis draft coming along?
transcript_lines.text_zh: Liam，你这周几乎没离开过书桌。你的毕业论文初稿写得怎么样了？

transcript_lines.speaker: Liam
transcript_lines.text: Slowly. The more anxious I get about the deadline, the longer I stare at the screen without writing a single clear paragraph.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 进展很慢。我越对截止日期感到焦虑，就越长时间盯着屏幕却写不出一段通顺的话。

transcript_lines.speaker: Grace
transcript_lines.text: Have you tried the campus counseling center's walking club? A group of us meet outside the botanical garden every Tuesday and Thursday at four.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 你试过学校心理咨询中心的散步小组吗？我们每周二和周四下午四点在植物园门口集合。

transcript_lines.speaker: Liam
transcript_lines.text: A walking club sounds nice, though I'm definitely not up for competitive jogging or forced group icebreakers right now.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 散步小组听起来不错，不过我现在可没精力参加竞技慢跑或者尴尬的小组破冰游戏。

transcript_lines.speaker: Grace
transcript_lines.text: Don't worry--there's no running and no awkward speeches. The only rule is keeping phones silenced inside backpacks for thirty minutes while we stroll.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 放心吧，不用跑步也不用尴尬发言。唯一的规定是在三十分钟散步期间把手机静音放进背包里。

transcript_lines.speaker: Liam
transcript_lines.text: No phones and no pressure? Count me in for Thursday at four. Maybe stepping outside will finally unstick my introduction.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 不用看手机也没压力？那算我一个，周四下午四点见。没准出去走走真能让我把引言写顺。

questions.stem: What difficulty is Liam experiencing with his senior thesis?
options: His computer crashed and deleted his introduction.
Anxiety makes him stare at his screen without making progress.
He lost all his research notes inside the botanical garden.
His advisor moved the final deadline forward by two weeks.
questions.answer: Anxiety makes him stare at his screen without making progress.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Slowly. The more anxious I get about the deadline, the longer I stare at the screen without writing a single clear paragraph.

questions.key_evidence_line: The more anxious I get about the deadline, the longer I stare at the screen without writing a single clear paragraph.
questions.explanation_zh: 第2句 Liam 描述焦虑导致的写作卡顿：越焦虑，盯着屏幕的时间越长，却写不出一段像样的文字。
distractor_reasons: 错误：文中未提电脑崩溃丢稿。
正确：精确概括第2句焦虑引发的卡壳状态。
错误：植物园是散步集合地点，并非丢笔记之处。
错误：文中未提导师提前截止日期。

questions.stem: What is the only rule of the counseling center's walking club?
options: Members must complete a thirty-minute brisk run together.
Everyone has to introduce their thesis topic during icebreakers.
Participants keep their phones silenced in their bags during the walk.
Walkers must attend both Tuesday and Thursday sessions every week.
questions.answer: Participants keep their phones silenced in their bags during the walk.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Don't worry--there's no running and no awkward speeches. The only rule is keeping phones silenced inside backpacks for thirty minutes while we stroll.

questions.key_evidence_line: The only rule is keeping phones silenced inside backpacks for thirty minutes while we stroll.
questions.explanation_zh: 第5句 Grace 用 The only rule 明确指出唯一规定：散步的三十分钟里把手机静音放进背包（keeping phones silenced inside backpacks）。
distractor_reasons: 错误：Grace 明确说 there's no running（不用跑步）。
错误：Grace 也否定了尴尬发言（no awkward speeches）。
正确：与第5句唯一规定完全吻合。
错误：Liam 只约了周四下午四点参加，并未强制周二周四全勤。

questions.stem: Where and when will Liam join the walking group?
options: Outside the counseling center on Tuesday at four.
Outside the botanical garden on Thursday at four.
Inside the campus library on Thursday morning.
At the athletic track on Tuesday afternoon.
questions.answer: Outside the botanical garden on Thursday at four.

evidence_anchor.text_span: A group of us meet outside the botanical garden every Tuesday and Thursday at four.

questions.key_evidence_line: meet outside the botanical garden every Tuesday and Thursday at four.
questions.explanation_zh: 综合第3句（集合地点在植物园外 outside the botanical garden，时间周二和周四四点）和第6句（Liam 说 Count me in for Thursday at four），确定为周四四点植物园外。
distractor_reasons: 错误：集合地点是植物园外，且 Liam 选的是周四。
正确：地点（botanical garden）与时间（Thursday at four）均准确。
错误：地点和时间均不符。
错误：并非在田径场集合。

listening_cases.title: Verifying AI Summaries in a Group Research Project
listening_cases.title_zh: 长对话：核查小组作业中 AI 总结引发的数据失真问题

transcript_lines.speaker: Nora
transcript_lines.text: Kevin, thanks for uploading the literature notes early, though I noticed something odd when comparing them with the original PDFs.
transcript_lines.text_zh: Kevin，谢谢你这么早上传文献笔记，不过我对照原始 PDF 时发现了一点奇怪的地方。

transcript_lines.speaker: Kevin
transcript_lines.text: Oh no, what happened? I was rushing between lab shifts, so I asked an AI tool to summarize five sociology articles for me.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 糟糕，怎么了？我当时在赶实验班次，就让一个 AI 工具帮我总结了五篇社会学论文。

transcript_lines.speaker: Nora
transcript_lines.text: Well, two survey percentages in your draft don't exist in the actual papers, and one author's conclusion was reversed.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 是这样的，你草稿里有两个调查百分比在原论文里根本不存在，而且还有一位作者的结论被说反了。

transcript_lines.speaker: Kevin
transcript_lines.text: Good thing you caught that before Monday's presentation! Should we throw away the whole outline and start over from scratch?
transcript_lines.text_zh: 幸亏你在周一汇报前发现了！那我们要把整份大纲扔掉从头再来吗？

transcript_lines.speaker: Nora
transcript_lines.text: No need to scrap the theme structure. Let's split the five articles tonight, verify every statistic directly against the PDFs, and replace fabricated lines.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 没必要推翻主题框架。我们今晚把这五篇论文分一下工，对照 PDF 逐条核实统计数据，替换掉编造的句子。

transcript_lines.speaker: Kevin
transcript_lines.text: Agreed. Also, Professor Wu's syllabus requires a short note explaining which tools were used for brainstorming, so let's include that too.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 同意。另外吴教授的课程大纲要求附一段简短说明，交代构思阶段用了哪些工具，我们也一并加上吧。

questions.stem: What errors did Nora discover in Kevin's literature notes?
options: Missing bibliography pages and broken web links.
Non-existent survey percentages and a reversed author conclusion.
Duplicate paragraphs copied from another group's slides.
Spelling mistakes in five sociology professors' names.
questions.answer: Non-existent survey percentages and a reversed author conclusion.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Well, two survey percentages in your draft don't exist in the actual papers, and one author's conclusion was reversed.

questions.key_evidence_line: two survey percentages in your draft don't exist in the actual papers, and one author's conclusion was reversed.
questions.explanation_zh: 第3句 Nora 指出 AI 总结的两类严重错误：两个调查百分比在原文不存在（don't exist -> non-existent），以及一位作者结论被颠倒（reversed）。
distractor_reasons: 错误：文中未提参考文献页缺失或链接失效。
正确：精确对应第3句发现的两处核心事实错误。
错误：未提抄袭其他小组幻灯片。
错误：未提教授姓名拼写错误。

questions.stem: How do Nora and Kevin decide to fix the draft tonight?
options: Discard the entire outline and write a new topic from scratch.
Ask a different AI tool to recheck the five articles automatically.
Divide the five PDFs to verify every statistic and fix false claims.
Postpone Monday's sociology presentation until next month.
questions.answer: Divide the five PDFs to verify every statistic and fix false claims.

evidence_anchor.text_span: No need to scrap the theme structure. Let's split the five articles tonight, verify every statistic directly against the PDFs, and replace fabricated lines.

questions.key_evidence_line: Let's split the five articles tonight, verify every statistic directly against the PDFs, and replace fabricated lines.
questions.explanation_zh: 第5句 Nora 否定了推翻重写的提议，决定两人分读五篇原文 PDF（split the five articles），逐项核对数据并替换虚构内容。
distractor_reasons: 错误：Nora 明确说 No need to scrap the theme structure。
错误：她们决定人工对照原始 PDF 核查，而非再用另一个 AI。
正确：divide 同义替换 split，直接对应第5句行动方案。
错误：文中未提推迟周一汇报。

questions.stem: What requirement in Professor Wu's syllabus does Kevin remind Nora about?
options: Students must submit five printed PDFs alongside the slides.
Groups must add a note disclosing tools used for brainstorming.
Every presentation must avoid quoting any statistical surveys.
Lab assistants must sign off on all group literature drafts.
questions.answer: Groups must add a note disclosing tools used for brainstorming.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Also, Professor Wu's syllabus requires a short note explaining which tools were used for brainstorming, so let's include that too.

questions.key_evidence_line: Professor Wu's syllabus requires a short note explaining which tools were used for brainstorming
questions.explanation_zh: 第6句 Kevin 补充课程规范：吴教授大纲要求附简短说明，披露构思阶段使用了哪些工具（which tools were used for brainstorming）。
distractor_reasons: 错误：未要求提交五份纸质打印版 PDF。
正确：disclosing tools used for brainstorming 对应 explaining which tools were used for brainstorming。
错误：未禁止引用调查统计。
错误：未提及实验助教签字。

listening_cases.title: Social Jetlag and Consistent Wake Times
listening_cases.title_zh: 短文听力：睡眠科学——为何固定起床时间比周末补觉更关键

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: After five days of early morning lectures, many university students sleep until noon on Saturday and Sunday to pay back their sleep debt.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 上完五天早课后，许多大学生周六和周日会睡到中午，想以此偿还“睡眠债”。

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: Sleep researchers call this four-hour weekend shift social jetlag because shifting wake times mimics flying across four time zones every Friday night.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 睡眠研究人员将这种周末推迟四小时起床的现象称为“社交时差”，因为这相当于每周五晚跨四个时区飞行。

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: Instead of leaving students refreshed, late weekend mornings delay the body's natural evening sleep signal, making Sunday night insomnia far more likely.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 周末睡懒觉非但不能让人神清气爽，反而会推迟人体夜间的自然困意信号，使周日晚上更容易失眠。

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: Chronobiologists therefore advise waking within one hour of your weekday alarm and getting outdoor daylight within thirty minutes to anchor your internal clock.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 因此，时间生物学家建议周末起床时间与工作日闹钟相差不超过一小时，并在醒后三十分钟内接触户外自然光，以稳定生物钟。

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: If exhaustion remains heavy, a short twenty-minute early-afternoon nap restores alertness without disrupting Sunday night rest.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 如果仍感到疲惫，午后早些时候小睡二十分钟即可恢复清醒，还不会打乱周日晚间的睡眠。

questions.stem: Why do researchers compare sleeping until noon on weekends to jetlag?
options: Students often study on international flights during holidays.
Shifting wake times by four hours resembles crossing four time zones.
Dormitory rooms are too noisy after midday on Sundays.
Early morning lectures require waking up before sunrise.
questions.answer: Shifting wake times by four hours resembles crossing four time zones.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Sleep researchers call this four-hour weekend shift social jetlag because shifting wake times mimics flying across four time zones every Friday night.

questions.key_evidence_line: shifting wake times mimics flying across four time zones every Friday night.
questions.explanation_zh: 第2句用 because 解释“社交时差”得名原因：把起床时间推迟四小时，等同于每周五晚飞越四个时区（mimics flying across four time zones）。
distractor_reasons: 错误：并非真的乘国际航班。
正确：resembles crossing four time zones 准确转述 mimics flying across four time zones。
错误：文中未提宿舍噪音。
错误：未提早课需在日出前起床。

questions.stem: What negative effect can late weekend wake-ups cause?
options: They make falling asleep on Sunday night much harder.
They double the need for twenty-minute afternoon naps.
They completely erase memory of Friday morning lectures.
They prevent students from absorbing natural daylight.
questions.answer: They make falling asleep on Sunday night much harder.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Instead of leaving students refreshed, late weekend mornings delay the body's natural evening sleep signal, making Sunday night insomnia far more likely.

questions.key_evidence_line: delay the body's natural evening sleep signal, making Sunday night insomnia far more likely.
questions.explanation_zh: 第3句说明周末晚起的后果：推迟夜间自然困意信号，使周日晚上更容易失眠（Sunday night insomnia）。
distractor_reasons: 正确：make falling asleep on Sunday night much harder 准确转述 making Sunday night insomnia far more likely。
错误：20 分钟午睡是第5句推荐的补救方法，并非周末晚起的后果。
错误：文中未提遗忘周五早课内容。
错误：自然光是用来调节生物钟的，并非被阻止吸收。

questions.stem: What do chronobiologists recommend to keep one's internal clock steady?
options: Drinking strong coffee immediately after waking up.
Keeping weekend wake times within one hour of weekday schedules and stepping into daylight.
Sleeping four extra hours on Saturday mornings to repay sleep debt.
Taking a two-hour nap every Sunday evening.
questions.answer: Keeping weekend wake times within one hour of weekday schedules and stepping into daylight.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Chronobiologists therefore advise waking within one hour of your weekday alarm and getting outdoor daylight within thirty minutes to anchor your internal clock.

questions.key_evidence_line: advise waking within one hour of your weekday alarm and getting outdoor daylight within thirty minutes to anchor your internal clock.
questions.explanation_zh: 第4句用 therefore 总结科学建议：周末起床与工作日闹钟差距控制在 1 小时内，并在醒后 30 分钟内到户外晒太阳。
distractor_reasons: 错误：文中未提及喝咖啡。
正确：精确对应第4句的两个核心习惯。
错误：周六多睡四小时正是本文反对的“社交时差”做法。
错误：第5句推荐的是午后早些时候小睡 20 分钟，而非周日晚间睡两小时。

listening_cases.title: The Decoy Effect Behind Cafe Cup Pricing
listening_cases.title_zh: 短文听力：消费心理学——咖啡杯型定价背后的“诱饵效应”

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: Have you ever walked into a cafe intending to buy a small coffee, only to walk out holding a large cup instead?
transcript_lines.text_zh: 你是否曾走进咖啡店本想买小杯，结果却拿着大杯走了出来？

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: Often, the middle size on the menu is not meant to be popular at all; behavioral economists call it a decoy option.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 通常菜单上的中杯根本不是为了畅销而设；行为经济学家称之为“诱饵选项”。

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: When a small costs three dollars, a medium four fifty, and a large only five dollars, the large suddenly looks like a clever bargain.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 当小杯卖三美元、中杯四点五美元、而大杯只需五美元时，大杯突然看起来像是一笔精明的划算买卖。

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: Without that awkwardly priced middle option, most customers comparing only three dollars and five dollars would happily stick with the small.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 如果没有那个定价尴尬的中杯选项，大多数只在三美元和五美元之间做比较的顾客会愉快地选择小杯。

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: The simplest defense is asking yourself how much you would actually drink before comparing price tags.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 最简单的应对方法是在对比价签之前，先问问自己实际到底能喝多少。

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the medium-sized coffee in the pricing example?
options: To serve as the store's top-selling cup for regular commuters.
To make the large cup appear to be a much better deal.
To reduce plastic waste from oversized drink lids.
To help baristas measure exact milk portions quickly.
questions.answer: To make the large cup appear to be a much better deal.

evidence_anchor.text_span: When a small costs three dollars, a medium four fifty, and a large only five dollars, the large suddenly looks like a clever bargain.

questions.key_evidence_line: When a small costs three dollars, a medium four fifty, and a large only five dollars, the large suddenly looks like a clever bargain.
questions.explanation_zh: 结合第2、3句：中杯作为诱饵选项（decoy option），通过把中杯定价为 4.5 美元而大杯仅 5 美元，衬托出大杯像一个绝妙划算的买卖（clever bargain）。
distractor_reasons: 错误：第2句明确说中杯根本不是为了畅销而设（not meant to be popular at all）。
正确：make the large cup appear to be a much better deal 精准解释第2-3句的诱饵逻辑。
错误：文中未提塑料盖环保问题。
错误：文中未提咖啡师量取牛奶。

questions.stem: What would most customers likely do if the medium option were removed?
options: Walk out of the cafe without buying anything.
Pay five dollars for the large cup even faster.
Stay with the three-dollar small size.
Ask the cafe to add an extra-large cup.
questions.answer: Stay with the three-dollar small size.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Without that awkwardly priced middle option, most customers comparing only three dollars and five dollars would happily stick with the small.

questions.key_evidence_line: Without that awkwardly priced middle option, most customers comparing only three dollars and five dollars would happily stick with the small.
questions.explanation_zh: 第4句使用虚拟条件 Without that awkwardly priced middle option 明确指出：没有中杯对比时，多数人会选择 3 美元的小杯（stick with the small）。
distractor_reasons: 错误：顾客仍会买小杯，不会空手离开。
错误：没有诱饵衬托，大杯反而显得贵，不会更快买大杯。
正确：stay with 同义替换 stick with。
错误：文中未提及超大杯。

questions.stem: How does the speaker suggest shoppers avoid falling for decoy pricing?
options: Decide how much coffee you truly need before checking prices.
Always calculate the price per ounce of every drink on the board.
Bring a reusable travel mug to receive a small discount.
Compare prices across at least three nearby coffee shops.
questions.answer: Decide how much coffee you truly need before checking prices.

evidence_anchor.text_span: The simplest defense is asking yourself how much you would actually drink before comparing price tags.

questions.key_evidence_line: The simplest defense is asking yourself how much you would actually drink before comparing price tags.
questions.explanation_zh: 第5句结尾给出应对策略：在比较价格标签前先问自己实际会喝多少（asking yourself how much you would actually drink before comparing price tags）。
distractor_reasons: 正确：与第5句建议完全一致。
错误：按单价计算反而更容易掉进“大杯单价更低”的心理陷阱，且文中未提。
错误：文中未提自带杯。
错误：文中未提货比三家。

listening_cases.title: Why Spaced Listening Beats Cramming Audio Tracks
listening_cases.title_zh: 短文听力：语言学习——为何分散短时精听胜过考前突击刷题

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: Before a major English listening exam, students frequently put on headphones for three straight hours on a single Sunday afternoon.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 在重要英语听力考试前，学生常常会在某个周日下午戴着耳机一口气连续听上三个小时。

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: Yet cognitive studies show that after roughly forty minutes of intense audio, ear fatigue sets in and learners miss subtle sound contrasts.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 然而认知研究表明，经历约四十分钟的高强度听力输入后，听觉疲劳就会出现，学习者会漏掉细微的语音对比。

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: By contrast, splitting the exact same practice into fifteen-minute sessions across several days produces stronger long-term recognition.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 相比之下，把完全相同的练习量拆分到几天里每次十五分钟完成，能形成更牢固的长期辨音记忆。

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: That happens because overnight sleep helps the brain sort new speech rhythms and store common word transitions more reliably.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 这是因为夜间睡眠能帮助大脑梳理新的语音节奏，更稳固地储存常见的词间转折与连读。

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: Even better, replaying one tough paragraph the next morning reveals how much faster your brain catches words it missed yesterday.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 更妙的是，第二天早上重听昨天觉得吃力的那一段，你会发现大脑捕捉漏听词汇的速度明显变快了。

questions.stem: What happens after about forty minutes of continuous listening practice?
options: Learners memorize subtle speech rhythms twice as fast.
Ear fatigue appears and students fail to notice fine sound differences.
Headphones begin distorting high-frequency spoken words.
The brain stores every new vocabulary item automatically.
questions.answer: Ear fatigue appears and students fail to notice fine sound differences.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Yet cognitive studies show that after roughly forty minutes of intense audio, ear fatigue sets in and learners miss subtle sound contrasts.

questions.key_evidence_line: after roughly forty minutes of intense audio, ear fatigue sets in and learners miss subtle sound contrasts.
questions.explanation_zh: 第2句用 Yet 转折指出连续精听约 40 分钟后的弊端：听觉疲劳出现（ear fatigue sets in），导致错过细微声音差异（miss subtle sound contrasts）。
distractor_reasons: 错误：不是记得更快，而是疲劳下降。
正确：fail to notice fine sound differences 精准转述 miss subtle sound contrasts。
错误：是人耳疲劳，而非耳机硬件失真。
错误：记忆巩固发生在夜间睡眠，不是连续听满40分钟。

questions.stem: Why do short practice sessions spread across multiple days work better?
options: Evening classes always use easier audio tracks than Sunday labs.
Nighttime sleep helps the brain organize speech patterns and transitions.
Fifteen-minute recordings contain fewer unfamiliar technical terms.
Students spend less total time practicing each week.
questions.answer: Nighttime sleep helps the brain organize speech patterns and transitions.

evidence_anchor.text_span: That happens because overnight sleep helps the brain sort new speech rhythms and store common word transitions more reliably.

questions.key_evidence_line: overnight sleep helps the brain sort new speech rhythms and store common word transitions more reliably.
questions.explanation_zh: 第4句用 That happens because 直接点明科学机制：夜间睡眠帮助大脑整理语音节奏并巩固词间转折记忆。
distractor_reasons: 错误：文中未对比晚课与周日实验室材料难度。
正确：organize speech patterns and transitions 对应 sort new speech rhythms and store common word transitions。
错误：第3句明确说是“完全相同的练习总量”（the exact same practice）拆分到多天。
错误：总量相同，并非总时间减少。

questions.stem: What practical tip does the speaker give at the end of the passage?
options: Avoid replaying difficult tracks once you finish checking answers.
Listen to three-hour podcasts right before falling asleep.
Revisit a challenging passage the next morning to test faster recognition.
Skip difficult paragraphs and focus only on familiar words.
questions.answer: Revisit a challenging passage the next morning to test faster recognition.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Even better, replaying one tough paragraph the next morning reveals how much faster your brain catches words it missed yesterday.

questions.key_evidence_line: replaying one tough paragraph the next morning reveals how much faster your brain catches words it missed yesterday.
questions.explanation_zh: 第5句提出实用建议：次日早晨重听前一天觉得吃力的段落（replaying one tough paragraph the next morning），可以体验大脑抓取漏词速度的提升。
distractor_reasons: 错误：原文恰恰鼓励第二天早上重听难点段落。
错误：原文反对连续三小时疲劳听音，且睡前听三小时与文意相悖。
正确：revisit a challenging passage 对应 replaying one tough paragraph。
错误：原文并非让跳过难段。

listening_cases.title: Twenty Minutes in Urban Parks Lowers Stress
listening_cases.title_zh: 短文听力：心理健康——城市绿地二十分钟如何有效降低压力激素

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: Many city residents assume they need an entire weekend camping trip in remote mountains to recover from weekday burnout.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 许多城市居民以为需要整个周末去偏远山区露营，才能从工作日的疲惫中恢复过来。

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: However, an eight-week field study tracking office workers found that spending just twenty minutes in an ordinary city park sharply reduced stress hormone levels.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 然而，一项为期八周、追踪上班族的实地研究发现，只需在普通城市公园待上二十分钟，压力激素水平就会大幅下降。

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: Interestingly, participants did not have to exercise hard; sitting quietly on a bench worked nearly as well as taking a slow stroll.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 有趣的是，参与者并不需要剧烈运动；静静坐在长椅上的效果几乎和慢步散心一样好。

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: The only condition that erased the benefit was scrolling through work messages or news feeds while outdoors.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 唯一会抵消这种减压效果的情况，是在户外时不停刷工作消息或新闻推送。

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: Researchers concluded that brief daily contact with trees and birdsong offers a realistic reset even during busy exam or work weeks.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 研究人员总结道，即使在繁忙的考试周或工作周，每天短暂接触树木和鸟鸣也能提供切实可行的心理重启。

questions.stem: What did the eight-week field study show about recovering from stress?
options: Remote mountain camping is the only effective cure for burnout.
Eight hours of park exercise is needed every weekend.
Twenty minutes in a local city park significantly lowers stress hormones.
Office workers feel more anxious inside quiet green spaces.
questions.answer: Twenty minutes in a local city park significantly lowers stress hormones.

evidence_anchor.text_span: However, an eight-week field study tracking office workers found that spending just twenty minutes in an ordinary city park sharply reduced stress hormone levels.

questions.key_evidence_line: spending just twenty minutes in an ordinary city park sharply reduced stress hormone levels.
questions.explanation_zh: 第1句引出常见误区（非得周末去偏远山区露营），第2句用 However 转折给出研究发现：普通城市公园待 20 分钟即可大幅降低压力激素。
distractor_reasons: 错误：这是第1句许多居民的误解（assume），被研究推翻。
错误：8 是研究周数（eight-week），20 分钟才是每次时长。
正确：sharply reduced 同义替换为 significantly lowers。
错误：与实验结论完全相反。

questions.stem: What did researchers find about sitting on a park bench versus walking slowly?
options: Sitting quietly produced nearly the same stress-relief benefit as strolling.
Walking fast was required to see any drop in stress hormones.
Sitting on benches caused participants to check work messages.
Strolling worked only when paired with loud fitness music.
questions.answer: Sitting quietly produced nearly the same stress-relief benefit as strolling.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Interestingly, participants did not have to exercise hard; sitting quietly on a bench worked nearly as well as taking a slow stroll.

questions.key_evidence_line: sitting quietly on a bench worked nearly as well as taking a slow stroll.
questions.explanation_zh: 第3句说明减压并不依赖剧烈运动：安静坐在长椅上的效果几乎和慢步散步一样好（worked nearly as well as taking a slow stroll）。
distractor_reasons: 正确：精确对应第3句的对比结论。
错误：第3句明确指出 did not have to exercise hard。
错误：刷消息是第4句提到的另一独立干扰条件，并非坐长椅必然导致。
错误：文中未提健身音乐。

questions.stem: What behavior canceled out the calming benefit of visiting a park?
options: Listening to birdsong during exam weeks.
Visiting the same neighborhood park every day.
Scrolling through work messages or news feeds outdoors.
Resting on a bench without exercising.
questions.answer: Scrolling through work messages or news feeds outdoors.

evidence_anchor.text_span: The only condition that erased the benefit was scrolling through work messages or news feeds while outdoors.

questions.key_evidence_line: The only condition that erased the benefit was scrolling through work messages or news feeds while outdoors.
questions.explanation_zh: 第4句用 The only condition 指出唯一会消除减压效果的行为：在户外刷工作消息或新闻推送（erased the benefit -> canceled out the calming benefit）。
distractor_reasons: 错误：第5句指出接触树木和鸟鸣正是减压机制。
错误：每天去普通公园恰恰是有效做法。
正确：与第4句完全吻合。
错误：坐长椅休息同样有效，不会抵消效果。

listening_cases.title: Cool Pavements and Shade Trees Against Urban Heat
listening_cases.title_zh: 短文听力：城市降温和节能——反光路面与行道树如何缓解热岛效应

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: During heatwaves, dense city neighborhoods often stay several degrees warmer after sunset than nearby rural farmland.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 在热浪期间，人口密集的城市街区日落后的温度往往比附近农田高出好几度。

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: A major culprit is dark asphalt streets, which absorb up to ninety percent of incoming solar heat and release it slowly into the night air.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 主要元凶之一是深色沥青路面，它会吸收高达百分之九十的太阳热量，并在夜间缓慢释放到空气中。

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: To fight this heat-island effect, several warm-climate cities are sealing streets with pale mineral coatings that bounce sunlight back into space.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 为对抗这种热岛效应，多个气候炎热的城市正在给街道涂覆浅色矿物涂层，将阳光反射回太空。

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: Early tests cut pavement surface temperatures by six degrees, yet planners warn that reflective streets alone can bounce glare onto walkers at noon.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 早期测试使路面温度降低了六摄氏度，但规划师提醒，单靠反光路面会在正午把眩光反射到行人身上。

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: Therefore, urban foresters pair cool coatings with broad-canopy street trees, delivering shade for pedestrians while reducing indoor air-conditioning demand.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 因此，城市林务人员将降温涂层与宽树冠行道树搭配使用，既为行人遮阴，又降低了室内空调需求。

questions.stem: Why do dense urban streets remain warm long after sunset?
options: Dark asphalt absorbs most solar heat and releases it gradually at night.
Rural farmland blocks cool evening winds from entering cities.
Indoor air conditioners blow cold air onto mineral sidewalks.
Street trees trap warm daytime air underneath their branches.
questions.answer: Dark asphalt absorbs most solar heat and releases it gradually at night.

evidence_anchor.text_span: A major culprit is dark asphalt streets, which absorb up to ninety percent of incoming solar heat and release it slowly into the night air.

questions.key_evidence_line: dark asphalt streets, which absorb up to ninety percent of incoming solar heat and release it slowly into the night air.
questions.explanation_zh: 第2句指出热岛元凶（major culprit）：深色沥青路面吸收高达 90% 的太阳热量并在夜晚缓慢释放（gradually 对应 slowly）。
distractor_reasons: 正确：精确对应第2句的热岛成因。
错误：文中未提农田阻挡凉风。
错误：未提空调向人行道吹冷风。
错误：行道树是降温方案，不是夜间高温元凶。

questions.stem: What drawback do planners warn about when pale reflective coatings are used alone?
options: They wash away completely during the first summer storm.
They raise pavement surface temperatures by six degrees.
They reflect uncomfortable midday glare onto pedestrians.
They cost ninety percent more than rebuilding asphalt roads.
questions.answer: They reflect uncomfortable midday glare onto pedestrians.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Early tests cut pavement surface temperatures by six degrees, yet planners warn that reflective streets alone can bounce glare onto walkers at noon.

questions.key_evidence_line: yet planners warn that reflective streets alone can bounce glare onto walkers at noon.
questions.explanation_zh: 第4句用 yet planners warn 引出单独使用浅色涂层的缺陷：正午时会把刺眼眩光反射到行人身上（bounce glare onto walkers at noon）。
distractor_reasons: 错误：文中未提被雨水冲刷殆尽。
错误：涂层是降低了（cut）六度，不是升高六度。
正确：pedestrians 同义替换 walkers，midday 对应 at noon。
错误：90% 是沥青吸热比例，不是造价比例。

questions.stem: Why do urban foresters combine pale road coatings with broad-canopy street trees?
options: To shade walkers while cutting indoor air-conditioning demand.
To keep asphalt streets dark enough for night drivers.
To replace mineral coatings in rural farming areas.
To block all sunlight from reaching rooftop solar panels.
questions.answer: To shade walkers while cutting indoor air-conditioning demand.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Therefore, urban foresters pair cool coatings with broad-canopy street trees, delivering shade for pedestrians while reducing indoor air-conditioning demand.

questions.key_evidence_line: delivering shade for pedestrians while reducing indoor air-conditioning demand.
questions.explanation_zh: 第5句结尾给出组合方案的双重效果：既为行人遮阴（shade for pedestrians），又减少室内空调耗电需求（reducing indoor air-conditioning demand）。
distractor_reasons: 正确：直接对应第5句的双重作用。
错误：目的是降温遮阴，并非让路面变黑。
错误：农村农田本就没有热岛问题，文中未提。
错误：文中未提屋顶光伏板。

listening_cases.title: Ferry Passengers Help Track Sea Turtle Migrations
listening_cases.title_zh: 短文听力：海洋保护与公民科学——渡轮乘客照片助力追踪海龟迁徙

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: Tracking ocean animals across thousands of kilometers is costly when scientists rely solely on specialized research vessels.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 如果科学家完全依赖专用科考船，在数千公里海域追踪海洋动物的成本会非常高昂。

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: To widen their reach, coastal biologists launched a smartphone app inviting daily ferry passengers to photograph sea turtles spotted near harbor routes.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 为了扩大监测范围，沿海生物学家推出一款手机应用，邀请日常渡轮乘客拍摄在港口航线附近看到的海龟。

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: Although casual riders sometimes mislabel species, every uploaded photo includes automatic time and location tags that experts review before entering the database.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 尽管普通乘客有时会标错物种名称，但每张上传照片都带有自动时间戳和位置标签，专家会在录入数据库前逐一复核。

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: Over three summers, four thousand verified sightings helped researchers detect a shift in turtle feeding grounds toward cooler northern seagrass beds.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 历经三个夏季，四千条经核实的目击记录帮助研究人员发现海龟觅食地正转向更凉爽的北部海草床。

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: Ferry operators now use those seasonal maps to slow vessels in key feeding corridors during peak migration weeks.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 渡轮运营方如今利用这些季节性分布图，在迁徙高峰周降低船只在核心觅食通道的航速。

questions.stem: Why did coastal biologists ask ferry passengers to upload sea turtle photos?
options: Dedicated research ships are expensive and limited in coverage.
Ferry passengers are trained marine biologists on holiday.
Satellite tags stopped working in northern seagrass beds.
Tourists complained that harbor ferries sailed too slowly.
questions.answer: Dedicated research ships are expensive and limited in coverage.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Tracking ocean animals across thousands of kilometers is costly when scientists rely solely on specialized research vessels.

questions.key_evidence_line: Tracking ocean animals across thousands of kilometers is costly when scientists rely solely on specialized research vessels.
questions.explanation_zh: 结合第1、2句：单靠专用科考船（specialized research vessels）既昂贵（costly）覆盖范围又有限，因此科学家开发应用动员渡轮乘客扩大追踪范围（widen their reach）。
distractor_reasons: 正确：research ships are expensive 对应 specialized research vessels... costly，limited in coverage 对应 to widen their reach。
错误：第3句称乘客是 casual riders（普通乘客），并非受过训练的生物学家。
错误：文中未提卫星标签失灵。
错误：渡轮减速是第5句的保护举措，并非乘客抱怨。

questions.stem: How do scientists ensure data accuracy even when passengers misidentify turtle species?
options: The app deletes photos taken by first-time ferry riders.
Biologists verify every time-and-location-tagged image before recording it.
Passengers must pass an online marine quiz before uploading.
Research vessels revisit each harbor route to re-photograph turtles.
questions.answer: Biologists verify every time-and-location-tagged image before recording it.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Although casual riders sometimes mislabel species, every uploaded photo includes automatic time and location tags that experts review before entering the database.

questions.key_evidence_line: every uploaded photo includes automatic time and location tags that experts review before entering the database.
questions.explanation_zh: 第3句用 Although 让步：虽然普通乘客可能标错物种，但照片自带时空标签且在入库前都由专家复核（experts review before entering the database）。
distractor_reasons: 错误：并不会删除首次上传者的照片。
正确：精确对应第3句专家复核机制。
错误：文中未提上传前需通过海洋测验。
错误：无需科考船重拍。

questions.stem: What trend did the verified turtle sightings reveal over three summers?
options: Sea turtles stopped feeding near coastal seagrass beds.
Harbor ferries frightened all turtles away from northern routes.
Turtles shifted their feeding areas toward cooler northern seagrass beds.
Four thousand turtles nested directly along city ferry docks.
questions.answer: Turtles shifted their feeding areas toward cooler northern seagrass beds.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Over three summers, four thousand verified sightings helped researchers detect a shift in turtle feeding grounds toward cooler northern seagrass beds.

questions.key_evidence_line: detect a shift in turtle feeding grounds toward cooler northern seagrass beds.
questions.explanation_zh: 第4句给出三年数据的生态发现：海龟觅食地正往更凉爽的北部海草床转移（shift in turtle feeding grounds toward cooler northern seagrass beds）。
distractor_reasons: 错误：海龟是转向北部海草床觅食，并非停止在海草床觅食。
错误：第5句说明渡轮会在觅食通道减速保护海龟，并非吓走全部海龟。
正确：与第4句科学发现完全吻合。
错误：four thousand 是经核实的目击记录条数（sightings），不是在码头筑巢的海龟数量。

listening_cases.title: Coastal Cities Pilot Floating Solar Farms in Unused Harbors
listening_cases.title_zh: 新闻听力：沿海城市在闲置港区试点水上光伏电站

transcript_lines.speaker: Anchor
transcript_lines.text: Two port authorities in eastern China have begun testing floating solar panels across sheltered harbor basins that are no longer needed for cargo ships.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 中国东部两家港务局已开始在不再停靠货轮的避风港池内测试水上光伏面板。

transcript_lines.speaker: Anchor
transcript_lines.text: Because coastal land near industrial zones is scarce and costly, engineers anchored modular arrays onto recyclable buoys that rise and fall gently with the tide.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 由于工业区附近的沿海土地稀缺且昂贵，工程师将模块化电池板固定在可回收浮筒上，使其随潮汐平稳升降。

transcript_lines.speaker: Anchor
transcript_lines.text: Sea breeze cooling naturally improves panel efficiency by roughly eight percent compared with inland rooftop systems during peak summer months.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 在盛夏高峰期，海风的自然降温使面板发电效率比内陆屋顶系统高出约百分之八。

transcript_lines.speaker: Anchor
transcript_lines.text: Clean power generated on site will directly charge electric tugboats and cold-storage warehouses inside the port district.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 现场产生的清洁电力将直接为港区内电动拖船和冷链仓库供电。

questions.stem: Where are the floating solar panels being tested?
options: In sheltered harbor basins no longer used by cargo ships.
On the roofs of inland agricultural warehouses.
Along crowded public beaches during the winter.
Inside deep-sea shipping lanes far from the coast.
questions.answer: In sheltered harbor basins no longer used by cargo ships.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Two port authorities in eastern China have begun testing floating solar panels across sheltered harbor basins that are no longer needed for cargo ships.

questions.key_evidence_line: Two port authorities in eastern China have begun testing floating solar panels across sheltered harbor basins that are no longer needed for cargo ships.
questions.explanation_zh: 首句明确交代试验地点为不再停靠货轮的避风港池（sheltered harbor basins）。
distractor_reasons: 正确：直接对应 sheltered harbor basins that are no longer needed for cargo ships。
错误：第3句将水上系统与内陆屋顶作对比，并非试验地点。
错误：文中未提海滩与冬季。
错误：远海主航道并不具备避风港池条件且文中未提。

questions.stem: Why did engineers choose floating arrays instead of building on nearby coastal land?
options: Coastal land near industrial areas is limited and expensive.
Local laws banned all rooftop solar panels last year.
Cargo vessels required taller cranes along the shore.
Saltwater corrosion makes land-based frames rust faster.
questions.answer: Coastal land near industrial areas is limited and expensive.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Because coastal land near industrial zones is scarce and costly, engineers anchored modular arrays onto recyclable buoys that rise and fall gently with the tide.

questions.key_evidence_line: Because coastal land near industrial zones is scarce and costly, engineers anchored modular arrays onto recyclable buoys that rise and fall gently with the tide.
questions.explanation_zh: 第2句指出因为工业区附近的沿海土地稀缺且昂贵（scarce and costly）。
distractor_reasons: 正确：limited and expensive 同义替换 scarce and costly。
错误：文中未提及屋顶禁令。
错误：文中未提及岸边起重机高度。
错误：文中未讨论陆地支架锈蚀对比。

questions.stem: What will the electricity produced by the harbor project mainly supply?
options: Electric tugboats and port cold-storage facilities.
High-speed passenger railways across the province.
Street lighting for nearby holiday resorts.
questions.answer: Electric tugboats and port cold-storage facilities.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Clean power generated on site will directly charge electric tugboats and cold-storage warehouses inside the port district.

questions.key_evidence_line: Clean power generated on site will directly charge electric tugboats and cold-storage warehouses inside the port district.
questions.explanation_zh: 末句提到所发电力将直接供应港内电动拖船（electric tugboats）和冷链仓库（cold-storage warehouses）。
distractor_reasons: 正确：直接对应末句供电去向。
错误：电能在港区就地消纳，未送往50英里外住宅。
错误：文中未提及高铁供电。
错误：文中未提及度假区路灯。

listening_cases.title: Switching a Campus Club Archive from Paper to Searchable Audio
listening_cases.title_zh: 长对话听力：把社团纸质档案升级为可检索有声口述史

transcript_lines.speaker: Maya
transcript_lines.text: Did you see the boxes of handwritten notebooks from the 1990s photography club in our storage closet?
transcript_lines.text_zh: 你看到我们储藏柜里那几箱上世纪九十年代摄影社团的手写笔记本了吗？

transcript_lines.speaker: Tom
transcript_lines.text: Yes, half the ink is fading, and nobody can find old darkroom tips unless they flip through three hundred pages.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 看到了，一半的墨水都在褪色，如果不翻上三百页，没人能找到当年的暗房技巧。

transcript_lines.speaker: Maya
transcript_lines.text: Instead of only scanning them as PDFs, what if we invite three retired alumni to record short twenty-minute interviews explaining the photos?
transcript_lines.text_zh: 与其只扫描成PDF，不如我们邀请三位退休校友录制二十分钟短访谈，请他们亲自讲解这些老照片，怎么样？

transcript_lines.speaker: Tom
transcript_lines.text: That would bring the history alive! Plus we can run speech transcription so future freshmen can search by keyword, like lens repair or night film.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 那会让历史鲜活起来！而且我们还能做语音转写，方便以后的大一新生按“镜头维修”或“夜景胶片”等关键词检索。

transcript_lines.speaker: Maya
transcript_lines.text: Let us apply for the library's mini-grant before Friday so we can borrow two studio microphones next month.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 我们周五前去申请图书馆的小额资助吧，这样下个月就能借两支录音室麦克风。

questions.stem: What problem do the old photography club notebooks currently have?
options: The ink is fading and entries are hard to search quickly.
They were accidentally donated to the city museum.
The storage closet suffered severe water damage last night.
Most pages were written in an unfamiliar foreign language.
questions.answer: The ink is fading and entries are hard to search quickly.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Yes, half the ink is fading, and nobody can find old darkroom tips unless they flip through three hundred pages.

questions.key_evidence_line: Yes, half the ink is fading, and nobody can find old darkroom tips unless they flip through three hundred pages.
questions.explanation_zh: Tom在第2句提到墨水正在褪色（ink is fading），且得翻几百页才能找内容（hard to search）。
distractor_reasons: 正确：与第2句褪色和翻页检索困难完全一致。
错误：笔记本仍在储藏柜中，未捐给市博物馆。
错误：对话未提及昨夜漏水。
错误：未提及外语书写问题。

questions.stem: What does Maya suggest doing alongside scanning the notebooks?
options: Recording brief interviews with three retired alumni about the photos.
Selling vintage darkroom equipment to raise club funds.
Reprinting every photograph as a large campus poster.
Closing the darkroom to create a quiet reading lounge.
questions.answer: Recording brief interviews with three retired alumni about the photos.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Instead of only scanning them as PDFs, what if we invite three retired alumni to record short twenty-minute interviews explaining the photos?

questions.key_evidence_line: Instead of only scanning them as PDFs, what if we invite three retired alumni to record short twenty-minute interviews explaining the photos?
questions.explanation_zh: Maya在第3句提议邀请三位退休校友录制20分钟访谈来讲解照片。
distractor_reasons: 正确：对应第3句 invite three retired alumni to record short twenty-minute interviews。
错误：未提出售暗房设备。
错误：未提印制校园大海报。
错误：未提关闭暗房。

questions.stem: Why does Tom support adding speech transcription to the audio files?
options: New club members will be able to look up topics by keyword.
The university requires subtitles on every social media post.
Retired alumni prefer reading printed scripts over listening.
It automatically fixes blurry scans from old cameras.
questions.answer: New club members will be able to look up topics by keyword.

evidence_anchor.text_span: That would bring the history alive! Plus we can run speech transcription so future freshmen can search by keyword, like lens repair or night film.

questions.key_evidence_line: That would bring the history alive! Plus we can run speech transcription so future freshmen can search by keyword, like lens repair or night film.
questions.explanation_zh: 第4句Tom指出语音转写能方便大一新生按关键词检索特定话题。
distractor_reasons: 正确：look up topics by keyword 对应 search by keyword。
错误：对话未提及社媒字幕规定。
错误：未提及校友个人阅读偏好。
错误：语音转写无法修复模糊扫描件。

listening_cases.title: How Quiet Reading Hour Transformed a Busy High-Speed Train Route
listening_cases.title_zh: 短文听力：静音阅读车厢时间如何改善繁忙高铁旅途体验

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: Last autumn, a regional rail operator introduced designated quiet reading coaches on its busiest three-hour morning commuter route.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 去年秋天，一家区域铁路运营商在其最繁忙的三小时早高峰通勤线路上推出了专用静音阅读车厢。

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: Passengers who choose the carriage agree to mute phone alerts, wear headphones for media, and keep voice calls for the vestibule between cars.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 选择该车厢的乘客需同意关闭手机提示音、使用耳机播放音视频，并前往车厢连接处接打电话。

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: Within six weeks, conductors noticed fewer seating disputes, while surveys showed commuters arrived at office meetings feeling noticeably calmer.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 仅六周时间，乘务员就发现座位争执减少，调查也显示通勤族到达办公会议时情绪明显更加平和。

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: Because demand exceeded expectations, the company plans to add small reading lamps and book-swap shelves to ten more trains this spring.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 由于需求超出预期，该公司计划今年春天在另外十趟列车上加装小型阅读灯和图书漂流架。

questions.stem: Where did the rail operator first introduce quiet reading coaches?
options: On its busiest three-hour morning commuter line.
On overnight sleeper trains across mountain regions.
Only in first-class dining cars during holidays.
On short subway shuttles inside airport terminals.
questions.answer: On its busiest three-hour morning commuter line.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Last autumn, a regional rail operator introduced designated quiet reading coaches on its busiest three-hour morning commuter route.

questions.key_evidence_line: Last autumn, a regional rail operator introduced designated quiet reading coaches on its busiest three-hour morning commuter route.
questions.explanation_zh: 首句指出最先在最繁忙的三小时早高峰通勤线路推行。
distractor_reasons: 正确：与首句 busiest three-hour morning commuter route 一致。
错误：未提山区夜班卧铺。
错误：未提节假日一等餐车。
错误：未提机场航站楼摆渡地铁。

questions.stem: What are passengers expected to do if they need to take a phone call?
options: Step into the vestibule area between train cars.
Whisper softly without leaving their window seat.
Wait until the train makes its final terminus stop.
Send a text message through the conductor's tablet.
questions.answer: Step into the vestibule area between train cars.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Passengers who choose the carriage agree to mute phone alerts, wear headphones for media, and keep voice calls for the vestibule between cars.

questions.key_evidence_line: Passengers who choose the carriage agree to mute phone alerts, wear headphones for media, and keep voice calls for the vestibule between cars.
questions.explanation_zh: 第2句明确规定接打电话需前往车厢连接处（vestibule between cars）。
distractor_reasons: 正确：直接对应 keep voice calls for the vestibule between cars。
错误：并非在靠窗座位轻声讲电话。
错误：未要求等列车到达终点站。
错误：未提使用乘务员平板发短信。

questions.stem: What change was observed six weeks after the quiet coaches launched?
options: Fewer disputes arose and passengers arrived calmer.
Ticket prices dropped sharply on afternoon departures.
Dining car coffee sales fell by nearly half.
More commuters missed their stations due to napping.
questions.answer: Fewer disputes arose and passengers arrived calmer.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Within six weeks, conductors noticed fewer seating disputes, while surveys showed commuters arrived at office meetings feeling noticeably calmer.

questions.key_evidence_line: Within six weeks, conductors noticed fewer seating disputes, while surveys showed commuters arrived at office meetings feeling noticeably calmer.
questions.explanation_zh: 第3句提到6周内座位争执减少且乘客抵站更从容平和。
distractor_reasons: 正确：总结自 fewer seating disputes 与 feeling noticeably calmer。
错误：未提及票价下调。
错误：未提及咖啡销量下降。
错误：未提及坐过站问题。

listening_cases.title: Urban Bakeries Turn Day-Old Sourdough into Brewing Ingredients
listening_cases.title_zh: 新闻听力：城市烘焙坊将隔夜酸面包转化为酿造原料

transcript_lines.speaker: Anchor
transcript_lines.text: A cooperative of neighborhood bakeries has teamed up with a local craft beverage maker to cut daily bread waste by over seventy percent.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 一个社区烘焙联盟与当地精酿饮品厂合作，将每日面包损耗削减了百分之七十以上。

transcript_lines.speaker: Anchor
transcript_lines.text: Instead of discarding unsold loaves at closing time, staff slice and toast remaining sourdough so it can replace one third of the barley malt used in small-batch fermentation.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 工作人员不再在打烊时丢弃未售出的面包，而是将剩余酸面包切片烘烤，用于替代小批量发酵中三分之一的大麦麦芽。

transcript_lines.speaker: Anchor
transcript_lines.text: To make pickups economical, an electric cargo van collects dried crumbs from twelve shops along a single evening loop.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 为降低清运成本，一辆电动货运厢车每晚沿单一环线从十二家门店回收干面包碎。

transcript_lines.speaker: Anchor
transcript_lines.text: Revenue from the recycled-grain drink helps subsidize free weekend baking workshops for community teenagers.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 这款再生谷物饮品的收益还将用于补贴面向社区青少年的免费周末烘焙工作坊。

questions.stem: What has the partnership between bakeries and the beverage maker achieved?
options: It reduced daily bread waste by more than seventy percent.
It opened twelve new craft drink shops near train stations.
It replaced all wheat flour with imported barley seeds.
It eliminated weekend opening hours for bakery staff.
questions.answer: It reduced daily bread waste by more than seventy percent.

evidence_anchor.text_span: A cooperative of neighborhood bakeries has teamed up with a local craft beverage maker to cut daily bread waste by over seventy percent.

questions.key_evidence_line: A cooperative of neighborhood bakeries has teamed up with a local craft beverage maker to cut daily bread waste by over seventy percent.
questions.explanation_zh: 新闻开篇点明双方合作将每日面包浪费削减超过 70%。
distractor_reasons: 正确：more than seventy percent 对应 over seventy percent。
错误：12家是参与合作的烘焙门店数量，非新开饮品店。
错误：是面包代替大麦麦芽，而非相反。
错误：周末开展青少年工作坊，并非取消营业。

questions.stem: How is the leftover sourdough processed before fermentation?
options: It is sliced and toasted to replace part of the barley malt.
It is frozen whole and shipped to overseas flour mills.
It is boiled in sugar syrup to feed sourdough starters.
It is ground directly into compost for rooftop gardens.
questions.answer: It is sliced and toasted to replace part of the barley malt.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Instead of discarding unsold loaves at closing time, staff slice and toast remaining sourdough so it can replace one third of the barley malt used in small-batch fermentation.

questions.key_evidence_line: Instead of discarding unsold loaves at closing time, staff slice and toast remaining sourdough so it can replace one third of the barley malt used in small-batch fermentation.
questions.explanation_zh: 第2句指出剩余面包先切片烘烤（slice and toast），再替代三分之一大麦麦芽。
distractor_reasons: 正确：精确对应第2句加工方式与比例。
错误：未提及冷冻出口至海外。
错误：未提及糖浆煮沸制作老面酵头。
错误：未提堆肥用途。

questions.stem: How is income from the recycled-grain beverage used?
options: To support free weekend baking classes for local teens.
To purchase diesel delivery trucks for suburbs.
To fund television advertisements during morning shows.
To refund customers who buy stale bread online.
questions.answer: To support free weekend baking classes for local teens.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Revenue from the recycled-grain drink helps subsidize free weekend baking workshops for community teenagers.

questions.key_evidence_line: Revenue from the recycled-grain drink helps subsidize free weekend baking workshops for community teenagers.
questions.explanation_zh: 末句说明饮品收益用于补贴面向青少年的免费周末烘焙工坊。
distractor_reasons: 正确：support free weekend baking classes 对应 subsidize free weekend baking workshops。
错误：配送用的是电动厢车且非柴油卡车。
错误：未提电视广告预算。
错误：未提网购退款。

listening_cases.title: Coordinating a Rain-Proof Community Night Market
listening_cases.title_zh: 长对话听力：为防雨升级改造社区夜市摊位与排班

transcript_lines.speaker: Sarah
transcript_lines.text: Looking at next Saturday's forecast, heavy showers might hit right when our outdoor food stalls open at six.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 看下周六的天气预报，强阵雨很可能会在六点露天小吃摊开市时准时袭来。

transcript_lines.speaker: Alex
transcript_lines.text: Good thing we kept the covered underground parking deck reserved as our Plan B venue.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 幸好我们一直把带有顶棚的地下停车层保留作为B方案备用场地。

transcript_lines.speaker: Sarah
transcript_lines.text: Moving there solves the rain issue, but ventilation could get stuffy if thirty vendors fire up gas grills indoors.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 搬到那儿确实解决了淋雨问题，但如果三十个摊位同时在室内开燃气烤炉，通风可能会很闷热。

transcript_lines.speaker: Alex
transcript_lines.text: You are right. Let us move only cold desserts, handicrafts, and acoustic music underground, while hot food trucks park just outside the loading bay canopy.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 你说得对。我们只把冷食甜点、手作摊和原声音乐挪到地下，热食餐车则停在装卸区雨棚正下方。

transcript_lines.speaker: Sarah
transcript_lines.text: Smart split. I will send map updates to all stall owners by noon tomorrow so nobody unloads in the wrong zone.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 分工太聪明了。我明天中午前把新版平面图发给所有摊主，避免有人在错误区域卸货。

questions.stem: Why are Sarah and Alex reviewing their venue plan for next Saturday?
options: Heavy rain is forecast around the six o'clock market opening.
The city council reduced parking spaces near the park.
Acoustic musicians requested louder stage amplifiers.
Over thirty new craft vendors signed up last minute.
questions.answer: Heavy rain is forecast around the six o'clock market opening.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Looking at next Saturday's forecast, heavy showers might hit right when our outdoor food stalls open at six.

questions.key_evidence_line: Looking at next Saturday's forecast, heavy showers might hit right when our outdoor food stalls open at six.
questions.explanation_zh: 首句Sarah提及天气预报显示下周六六点开市时可能有强阵雨。
distractor_reasons: 正确：与首句 heavy showers ... open at six 完全吻合。
错误：并非因为市政府削减车位。
错误：音乐人扩音设备在对话中未提。
错误：30位摊主是既有规模，并非临时加签。

questions.stem: What concern does Sarah raise about moving every stall into the parking deck?
options: Air circulation would suffer if thirty stalls cooked indoors.
Ceiling heights are too low for craft display banners.
Public buses cannot reach the underground entrance.
Security guards refuse to work past midnight on weekends.
questions.answer: Air circulation would suffer if thirty stalls cooked indoors.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Moving there solves the rain issue, but ventilation could get stuffy if thirty vendors fire up gas grills indoors.

questions.key_evidence_line: Moving there solves the rain issue, but ventilation could get stuffy if thirty vendors fire up gas grills indoors.
questions.explanation_zh: Sarah在第3句担心30个摊位室内生火会使通风变闷（ventilation could get stuffy）。
distractor_reasons: 正确：air circulation 对应 ventilation。
错误：未提横幅限高。
错误：未提公交接驳。
错误：未提保安加班问题。

questions.stem: How do the speakers solve the conflict between rain protection and cooking smoke?
options: They place crafts and cold foods underground and hot trucks under the loading bay canopy.
They postpone the entire market until the following sunny Sunday.
They cancel all hot food booths and refund vendor deposits.
They install twenty temporary plastic tents on the sports field.
questions.answer: They place crafts and cold foods underground and hot trucks under the loading bay canopy.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Good thing we kept the covered underground parking deck reserved as our Plan B venue.

questions.key_evidence_line: Good thing we kept the covered underground parking deck reserved as our Plan B venue.
questions.explanation_zh: 结合第2、4句，双方将手工艺和冷食放地下有顶棚车库，热食餐车移至室外装卸区雨棚下。
distractor_reasons: 正确：精准概括 Alex 第4句的分流方案。
错误：未推迟至周日。
错误：并未取消热食摊位。
错误：未提在运动场搭20顶塑料帐篷。

listening_cases.title: Why Seaweed Packaging Dissolves Safely in Warm Dishwater
listening_cases.title_zh: 短文听力：为何海藻基包装膜能在温水中无害溶解

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: Fast-food chains spend billions handling single-use sauce sachets that are too small and oily for standard recycling machines to sort.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 快餐连锁品牌每年花费巨资处理一次性酱料包，但它们因体积过小且带油渍而无法被常规回收机器分拣。

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: In response, marine biomaterials startups began pressing fast-growing brown kelp into thin, flavorless pouches that hold ketchup or chili oil at room temperature.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 为此，海洋生物材料初创企业开始将生长迅速的褐藻压制成薄而无味的包装袋，可在室温下盛装番茄酱或辣椒油。

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: Once emptied, the seaweed film dissolves completely in warm tap water within two minutes or breaks down in backyard soil in under six weeks.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 用完后，这种海藻膜可在两分钟内完全溶解于温自来水中，或在不到六周内于后院土壤中自然降解。

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: Because kelp farming absorbs excess coastal nitrogen without freshwater irrigation, nutritionists also view the crop as a climate-friendly raw material.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 由于褐藻养殖在无需淡水灌溉的情况下就能吸收沿岸过量氮元素，营养与环保专家也将其视为低碳原料。

questions.stem: Why are conventional single-use sauce sachets rarely recycled?
options: They are too tiny and greasy for sorting equipment to process.
Supermarkets charge extra fees to collect plastic wrappers.
Sauce manufacturers glue heavy paper labels over the plastic.
Local water plants refuse to wash stainless steel containers.
questions.answer: They are too tiny and greasy for sorting equipment to process.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Fast-food chains spend billions handling single-use sauce sachets that are too small and oily for standard recycling machines to sort.

questions.key_evidence_line: Fast-food chains spend billions handling single-use sauce sachets that are too small and oily for standard recycling machines to sort.
questions.explanation_zh: 首句指出传统酱料包太小且满是油污（too small and oily），常规回收设备无法分拣。
distractor_reasons: 正确：tiny and greasy 对应 small and oily。
错误：未提超市收费。
错误：未提厚纸标签。
错误：未提不锈钢容器。

questions.stem: What feature makes brown kelp suitable for holding ketchup or chili oil?
options: It forms a thin, flavorless pouch stable at room temperature.
It adds a mild roasted sea salt aroma to spicy dishes.
It freezes sauce instantly without electrical refrigeration.
It turns bright red to warn buyers of expired condiments.
questions.answer: It forms a thin, flavorless pouch stable at room temperature.

evidence_anchor.text_span: In response, marine biomaterials startups began pressing fast-growing brown kelp into thin, flavorless pouches that hold ketchup or chili oil at room temperature.

questions.key_evidence_line: In response, marine biomaterials startups began pressing fast-growing brown kelp into thin, flavorless pouches that hold ketchup or chili oil at room temperature.
questions.explanation_zh: 第2句表明褐藻可压成薄且无味（thin, flavorless）的袋子并在室温下保持稳定。
distractor_reasons: 正确：与第2句描述完全一致。
错误：明确说明包装袋是无味的（flavorless）。
错误：并未具备冷冻功能。
错误：并未变色报警。

questions.stem: How long does it take the emptied seaweed film to break down in warm tap water?
questions.answer: Within two minutes.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Once emptied, the seaweed film dissolves completely in warm tap water within two minutes or breaks down in backyard soil in under six weeks.

questions.key_evidence_line: Once emptied, the seaweed film dissolves completely in warm tap water within two minutes or breaks down in backyard soil in under six weeks.
questions.explanation_zh: 第3句区分了温水中溶解仅需两分钟（within two minutes），土壤降解则不超过六周。
distractor_reasons: 正确：温水溶解耗时对应 within two minutes。
错误：混淆时间单位。
错误：干扰项。
错误：不到六周是在后院土壤中降解的时间。

listening_cases.title: Municipal Libraries Introduce Musical Instrument Lending Shelves
listening_cases.title_zh: 新闻听力：市政图书馆推出乐器借阅专架

transcript_lines.speaker: Anchor
transcript_lines.text: Public libraries across three mid-sized cities have expanded beyond books by stocking acoustic guitars, ukuleles, and digital keyboards for free four-week loans.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 三座中型城市的公共图书馆不再局限于借书，新增了木吉他、尤克里里和电钢琴，提供免费四周借阅。

transcript_lines.speaker: Anchor
transcript_lines.text: Library directors noticed that many curious beginners give up on music before buying an expensive instrument they might rarely touch.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 馆长们发现许多心怀好奇的初学者常常因顾虑高昂购琴成本而在真正学琴前就放弃了。

transcript_lines.speaker: Anchor
transcript_lines.text: Each padded carrying case includes a clip-on tuner, spare strings, and a QR card linking to beginner chord videos filmed by local teachers.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 每个加厚琴包内都配有夹式调音器、备用琴弦以及链接本地老师录制的入门和弦视频二维码卡。

transcript_lines.speaker: Anchor
transcript_lines.text: Waitlists remain long, yet return checks show ninety-eight percent of instruments come back clean and undamaged.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 尽管排队预约名单依然很长，归还检查显示百分之九十八的乐器归还时干净且完好无损。

questions.stem: How long can patrons borrow an instrument from the participating libraries?
options: For four weeks free of charge.
For one weekend with a small deposit.
Only inside the library's practice rooms.
questions.answer: For four weeks free of charge.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Public libraries across three mid-sized cities have expanded beyond books by stocking acoustic guitars, ukuleles, and digital keyboards for free four-week loans.

questions.key_evidence_line: Public libraries across three mid-sized cities have expanded beyond books by stocking acoustic guitars, ukuleles, and digital keyboards for free four-week loans.
questions.explanation_zh: 首句指出提供免费的四周借期（free four-week loans）。
distractor_reasons: 正确：与首句 free four-week loans 一致。
错误：未提仅限周末及押金。
错误：未提整个学期。
错误：带有防撞琴包外借，非仅限馆内练习室。

questions.stem: What prompted library directors to launch the instrument collection?
options: Many beginners hesitate to pay for costly instruments just to try.
City schools lacked storage closets for marching band drums.
Music stores offered to donate damaged display keyboards.
Evening book clubs needed background music during readings.
questions.answer: Many beginners hesitate to pay for costly instruments just to try.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Library directors noticed that many curious beginners give up on music before buying an expensive instrument they might rarely touch.

questions.key_evidence_line: Library directors noticed that many curious beginners give up on music before buying an expensive instrument they might rarely touch.
questions.explanation_zh: 第2句表明许多初学者不愿先花高价买琴再去尝试，导致提前放弃。
distractor_reasons: 正确：精确反映第2句馆长的观察动机。
错误：未提校园行进乐队鼓室。
错误：未提乐器店捐赠破损琴。
错误：未提读书会配乐。

questions.stem: Where do the beginner chord videos linked on the QR card come from?
options: They were recorded by local music teachers.
They were licensed from a national television contest.
They are automatically translated from old radio tapes.
They are live streams hosted by library IT volunteers.
questions.answer: They were recorded by local music teachers.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Each padded carrying case includes a clip-on tuner, spare strings, and a QR card linking to beginner chord videos filmed by local teachers.

questions.key_evidence_line: Each padded carrying case includes a clip-on tuner, spare strings, and a QR card linking to beginner chord videos filmed by local teachers.
questions.explanation_zh: 第3句明确提到入门和弦视频由当地教师拍摄（filmed by local teachers）。
distractor_reasons: 正确：direct match with filmed by local teachers。
错误：未提全国电视比赛授权。
错误：未提广播录音转译。
错误：未提图书馆IT志愿者直播。

listening_cases.title: Designing Low-Glare Lighting for an Engineering Design Lab
listening_cases.title_zh: 长对话听力：为工科设计实验室定制低眩光阅读与绘图照明

transcript_lines.speaker: Dr. Lin
transcript_lines.text: Ever since we installed the bright white overhead LEDs in Lab 302, architecture students complain about headaches during late blueprint critiques.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 自从302实验室装了高亮度白光吸顶LED后，建筑系学生在晚间图纸讲评时一直反映头疼。

transcript_lines.speaker: Chloe
transcript_lines.text: I measured the glossy drafting tables yesterday—glare bounces straight off the tracing paper into their eyes.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 我昨天测了光面绘图桌——刺眼眩光会从硫酸纸上直接反射进眼睛里。

transcript_lines.speaker: Dr. Lin
transcript_lines.text: Before spending budget on replacing every ceiling panel, could we test indirect wall-wash strips combined with adjustable warm desk lamps?
transcript_lines.text_zh: 在花预算更换整套吸顶灯盘之前，我们能不能先测试间接洗墙灯带搭配可调节暖色台灯？

transcript_lines.speaker: Chloe
transcript_lines.text: Let us try that on the north bench row first! Students can dial color temperature warmer after seven p.m. while keeping crisp task lighting on models.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 先在北侧操作台那一排试点吧！晚上七点后学生可以把色温调暖，同时保持模型上的精准局部照明。

transcript_lines.speaker: Dr. Lin
transcript_lines.text: Great plan. Collect anonymous eye-comfort scores from twenty students after two weeks so we have real data for facilities management.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 方案很好。两周后收集二十位同学的匿名用眼舒适度评分，我们就能拿真实数据向后勤管理处申报了。

questions.stem: What complaint led Dr. Lin and Chloe to review the lab lighting?
options: Students get headaches from the bright overhead LEDs during evening reviews.
Broken ceiling fixtures leave half the drafting room in darkness.
Electricity bills doubled after adding extra desktop monitors.
Blueprint printers cannot match colors under dim yellow bulbs.
questions.answer: Students get headaches from the bright overhead LEDs during evening reviews.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Ever since we installed the bright white overhead LEDs in Lab 302, architecture students complain about headaches during late blueprint critiques.

questions.key_evidence_line: Ever since we installed the bright white overhead LEDs in Lab 302, architecture students complain about headaches during late blueprint critiques.
questions.explanation_zh: Dr. Lin开篇提到白光吸顶LED导致学生在晚间图纸讲评时头疼。
distractor_reasons: 正确：与首句 headaches during late blueprint critiques 一致。
错误：灯光问题是太亮刺眼而非昏暗损坏。
错误：未提及电费翻倍。
错误：尚未换用暖色照明时问题在于刺眼白光。

questions.stem: What did Chloe discover when measuring the drafting tables?
options: Glossy table surfaces and tracing paper reflect glare into students' eyes.
Wooden benches absorb too much light along the north wall.
Several wall outlets were overloaded by adjustable desk fans.
Morning sunlight fades ink sketches on architectural boards.
questions.answer: Glossy table surfaces and tracing paper reflect glare into students' eyes.

evidence_anchor.text_span: I measured the glossy drafting tables yesterday—glare bounces straight off the tracing paper into their eyes.

questions.key_evidence_line: I measured the glossy drafting tables yesterday—glare bounces straight off the tracing paper into their eyes.
questions.explanation_zh: 第2句Chloe测出光线经光面桌与硫酸纸反射形成眩光直射双眼。
distractor_reasons: 正确：对应 glare bounces straight off the tracing paper。
错误：未提木质长凳吸光。
错误：未提插座与台扇过载。
错误：讲的是晚间讲评室内灯光，非晨光晒褪色。

questions.stem: Why does Dr. Lin propose testing wall-wash strips and desk lamps first?
options: To avoid wasting budget replacing all ceiling fixtures before testing.
Because facilities management forbade buying new white LEDs.
To turn Lab 302 into a photography studio next semester.
Because architectural models must be viewed in total darkness.
questions.answer: To avoid wasting budget replacing all ceiling fixtures before testing.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Before spending budget on replacing every ceiling panel, could we test indirect wall-wash strips combined with adjustable warm desk lamps?

questions.key_evidence_line: Before spending budget on replacing every ceiling panel, could we test indirect wall-wash strips combined with adjustable warm desk lamps?
questions.explanation_zh: 第3句表示“在花预算更换全部天花板灯盘之前先做局部测试”，体现成本效益意识。
distractor_reasons: 正确：对应 Before spending budget on replacing every ceiling panel。
错误：并未禁止购买白光灯。
错误：实验室仍用于工科/建筑设计，不改摄影棚。
错误：仍需清晰局部台灯照明模型。

listening_cases.title: Community Seed Libraries Guard Local Vegetable Varieties
listening_cases.title_zh: 短文听力：社区种子图书馆如何守护本地抗旱蔬菜品种

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: Unlike supermarket seed racks filled with a handful of uniform commercial hybrids, neighborhood seed libraries preserve locally adapted varieties that thrive in regional soils.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 与超市里仅有少数几种标准化商业杂交品种的货架不同，社区种子图书馆保存了更适应当地土壤的本土品种。

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: Amateur gardeners check out three labeled paper envelopes in March without spending a cent.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 业余园艺爱好者每年三月可免费借出三个贴好标签的纸信封种子。

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: After the autumn harvest, borrowers dry seeds from their healthiest plants and return a fresh batch alongside notes on drought tolerance and taste.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 秋收之后，借阅者从最健壮的植株上晾干留种，在归还新一批种子的同时附上关于耐旱性与口感的记录笔记。

transcript_lines.speaker: Narrator
transcript_lines.text: Over five years, one valley network built a shared catalog of forty-two resilient bean and tomato lines suited to unpredictable summer heat.
transcript_lines.text_zh: 五年间，一个河谷协作网络建立了包含四十二种耐酷暑豆类与番茄品系的共享目录。

questions.stem: How do neighborhood seed libraries differ from supermarket seed racks?
options: They keep locally adapted varieties rather than uniform commercial hybrids.
They sell organic vegetables harvested by library staff.
They focus solely on ornamental flowers for city balconies.
They charge annual membership fees to commercial farmers.
questions.answer: They keep locally adapted varieties rather than uniform commercial hybrids.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Unlike supermarket seed racks filled with a handful of uniform commercial hybrids, neighborhood seed libraries preserve locally adapted varieties that thrive in regional soils.

questions.key_evidence_line: Unlike supermarket seed racks filled with a handful of uniform commercial hybrids, neighborhood seed libraries preserve locally adapted varieties that thrive in regional soils.
questions.explanation_zh: 首句将两者对比：社区种子图书馆保存本地适应性强的地方品种，而非少数商业杂交品种。
distractor_reasons: 正确：与首句对比结构完全对应。
错误：图书馆出借种子而非售卖蔬菜。
错误：关注点在于菜豆、番茄等耐旱蔬菜品种。
错误：三月借出免费（without spending a cent）。

questions.stem: How much do gardeners pay when checking out three seed packets in March?
options: Nothing at all; borrowing is free.
Ten percent of their autumn market sales.
Only the postage cost of paper envelopes.
questions.answer: Nothing at all; borrowing is free.

evidence_anchor.text_span: Amateur gardeners check out three labeled paper envelopes in March without spending a cent.

questions.key_evidence_line: Amateur gardeners check out three labeled paper envelopes in March without spending a cent.
